target_customer: Developers and teams using Claude Code who want lower token cost and faster runs
problem: Claude Code usage consumes many tokens through tool calls and context growth. WOZCODE replaces tool calls with custom tools to cut cost and time.
business_model: Plugin for an AI coding agent, subscription or usage pricing, details not found

founders.name: Ben Collins
founders.background_notes: Friend of co-founder for over 13 years per launch post.

founders.name: Brad Eckert
founders.background_notes: Led 30+ engineers, 25+ patents per YC profile.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building tools that reduce tool calls and context size for a coding agent is real engineering, with benchmark validation, but sits on top of someone else's agent.

defensibility.rationale: A plugin on a platform whose owner can absorb the gains, and many open source token saving plugins exist in 2026.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The acquirer was a bank, not a platform owner, and bought the team more than the plugin per one report. Whether Anthropic absorbed the gains is not sourced.

market_need_then: AI coding agent bills were a visible pain; many guides and tools on cutting Claude Code token use appeared, showing demand.

branding.domain_note: Product site wozcode.com; company domain history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Casual and confident, short outcome headlines such as cut your Claude Code costs in half

branding.community_and_virality: Launched on Product Hunt; listed on several developer directories

brand_strength.rationale: Shares its name with Steve Wozniak's nickname and the Woz U education brand, which is confusable; no source shows a distinct brand following.

outcome_analysis: Woz joined YC in Winter 2025 with two MIT trained founders, raised 6 million dollars in seed funding in October 2025 and then agreed to be bought by Kapital for 30 million dollars in cash and stock in October 2026. One report says the deal is mainly for the team and that the plugin is the smaller asset. The result is a soft exit for a small team in a thin layer on top of a platform.
